Å tjänstens vägnar fick @mwj65 möjlighet att återigen besöka fantastiska och unika @arcticbath_sweden. Det här är verkligen en anläggning utöver det vanliga. 🤩 

Delägaren @speteng berättar om historien bakom skapelsen, och att arkitekturen är en hyllning till regionens timmerarv och Luleälvens historia. 🪵 

Vi tar det från början. I Harads, mitt i den vackra norrbottniska naturen, ligger @arcticbath_sweden. Det är en plats där design, historia och natur bokstavligen flyter ihop på Luleälven. 

Den cirkulära byggnaden med restaurang, bastu och kallbad är ritad av arkitekten Bertil Harström. Byggnaden är inspirerad av den gamla timmerflottningen på Luleälven och ser ut som en timmerbröt mitt ute i vattnet. Riktigt häftigt! 👌

Stugorna på vatten är ritad av tornedalingen Johan Kauppi. Stugornas lutande, nästan ”på väg att falla” form har kopplats till de äldre flottarstugorna längs älven, vars fundament kunde börja ge efter och få husen att luta pga vatten, is, snö och älvens krafter. 

Landstugorna är ritad av AnnKathrin Lundqvist. Deras triangulära form är inspirerad av ett traditionellt verktyg som flottarna använde för att lösa upp timmerbrötar, en så kallad flottningshake. Verktyget hade en spetsig form som användes för att få isär stockarna när de hade fastnat. 

Allt det här är så häftigt och coolt! 😍 På sommaren flyter @arcticbath_sweden på älven. På vintern fryser det fast i isen. Och däremellan väntar kallbad, bastu, stillhet och den magiska känslan av att vara nära naturen. 😇

@discoveringtellus har varit här och vi kan konstatera att besöksnäringen är som bäst när arkitektur, historia och natur får skapa något riktigt unikt. 💙❄️

caption:
Saunasaari was built for one thing: sauna.
Around the turn of the millennium, the City of Helsinki decided this little island – then called Pikkusaari – should become a sauna village. So they went looking for someone to build it. That someone was Rainer Hanhilahti, who knew a thing or two about tourism and traditional log building. Back then, the island had three saunas: Perinnesavu, Haapasavu and Pihasavu.

As the island started hosting more private events, Pihasavu was eventually turned into a kitchen and dining space.  Today, from spring to autumn, most of the cooking happens outside, over an open fire.

More than 20 years later, the idea is still quite simple: sauna, sea and something seasonal and delicious to eat afterwards.

we just got back from the International Sauna Congress in Oslo and we have a lot to say. 🔥🌊

it all opened in Oslo City Hall in the same room where the Nobel Peace Prize is handed out and left us with our favorite line of the trip: “there’s no war in a sauna.”

about 500 sauna people from around the world spent three days on culture, health, architecture and the future of the waterfront. 

Oslo, Copenhagen, Paris, Helsinki and Melbourne are all using saunas to bring people back to the water. 
once saunas show up on a waterfront, everything follows:

the robes, the community, the music, the food, the swimmers. city leaders who started out skeptical came around once they saw it.

huge thanks to @saunacongress2026 and a shoutout to @saunachannel for premiering Fire Between the Fjords.

the movement is global and we are happy to say that portland is part of it. we came home fired up about what we’re building here, on and off the water. 💧

caption:
Lonely in London? Sauna as the new place to socialise... 🌀

London can be such a fun and busy city. But, despite being surrounded by so many people, us Londoners are feeling increasingly isolated.

Many of us are working from home. Typical social spaces revolve around alcohol and aren’t designed to help you meet new people. So, we’ve built a new kind of space...

When we opened last Autumn, we were chasing a dream we couldn’t quite find anywhere else.

A place to connect with people, listen to amazing music, and leave feeling really (really) good. All without the pressure to consume alcohol or any of nightlife’s other excesses.

Don’t get us wrong, London is home to SO many amazing independent nighttime venues, with incredible music programming. These venues still hold a special place in our hearts.

But the loneliness epidemic is real, and we wanted to create a space that truly brings people together. 

So whether you sauna for your physical health, mental health, or social connection - come alone or with friends. Everyone is welcome.

We can’t wait to meet you 🫧

While living in London, where I had spent most of my life, I spent almost a decade living on my own. My girlfriends all had children around the same time, and I was left feeling isolated and very alone. As much as I tried to fill my days with connection, I found it so hard to walk into a pub alone, have a drink, and then leave alone. I would often drink too much to lose my inhibitions and pluck up the courage to talk to people, only to feel rejected by the clique groups I found there.

It became a vicious circle that slowly ate away at my confidence. Years later, now happily married, I hear my story repeated over and over again by others. It’s a pandemic all of its own.

I have come to this sauna community with love and openness, both for myself and for others. Sauna is for everyone, and good heat knows no borders, religions, skin colours, or cultures. Just warmth and connection.

Prest er eit fjell som ligg i Aurland, der du har utsikt over Aurlandsfjorden.

The hike starts at around 800 meter above sea levels, and you hike to the viewpoint at Røyrgind, 1363 meter above sea level. 

Turen startar på rundt 800 meter over havet, og toppen ein går mot heiter Røyrgrind, 1363 meter over havet.

caption:
Relatable? 🫠

That post sauna wobble can catch you off guard. It’s usually a sign to slow down and listen to your body. 

Why it happens:
- Heat widens your blood vessels → blood pressure can drop.
- You’ve been sweating → fluid levels are down.
- You’ve lost electrolytes → sodium + potassium need replacing.
- You stand up too quickly → hello, wobble.
- And remember, sauna-ing on an empty stomach can make feeling weak or lightheaded more likely. 

Here are our tips:
- Cool down slowly - spend some time resting outside before the plunge. 
- Keep hydrating.
- Electrolytes.
- Go at your own pace, especially if you’re new to sauna.
- Don’t go in starving - a light snack beforehand is always good. 

Be gone, wobble! 😋

Banya has been practised for over a thousand years across Eastern Europe - not only as a way of washing, but as a ritual space for initiation, transition, and transformation. A place where people return to warmth, water, and community as a form of deep care.

Sasha is a banya and sauna guide who grew up in the Ural Mountains in Russia, attending banya every Sunday for fifteen years. She has since trained with a Russian steam master and completed a course in ceremonial banya in the Mordvin tradition, bringing a lifelong and deeply researched relationship with these practices.

In this small and intimate session for women and non-binary people, Sasha guides three steam cycles through gentle 60–80°C heat, working with intention setting, breathwork, salt scrubbing, fragrant herbal infusions, and parenie with oak or birch whisks. A space to rest, nourish, and find collective care.

caption:
Explore the elements to facilitate connection: Yoga | Sauna | Cold Immersion 🧘

As we transition from the energetic yang of summer to the reflective yin of autumn, enter this season with intention through this ritual of connection.

💧When? Saturday 17th October, 10am-12.30pm
💧Where? Camberwell

The first hour is outdoor yoga in the park (or in our yurt if the weather is bad), where you’ll slow down your mind and invite stillness through meditation, breathwork and flowy movement.

The next hour and a half is a free-flow sauna session. Move between the sauna and cold immersion at your own pace to explore a deeper connection with your body across different environments. Cold immersion is always optional.

Common Yoga is a kind community built on compassion toward yourself and others. Come as you are, no experience needed.

Bring a yoga mat, comfortable clothes, and your sauna essentials: swimsuit, two towels, water bottle, and flip flops/sliders.
